episode_title: How I Reversed My Type 2 Diabetes

stories.summary: Amit was diagnosed with Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c 7.7) and hypertension. His doctor gave him Metformin and vague advice. Amit used a Continuous Glucose Monitor (CGM), adopted Keto and Intermittent Fasting (OMAD), and reversed his HbA1c to 5.7. He realized that 'sugar is poison' and that standard medical advice is often outdated.
stories.insight: Type 2 Diabetes is reversible through diet. 'Know Thyself' using tools like CGM is more effective than generic advice.

stories.summary: Ajay ate a meal of Sugar (Gatorade), White Rice, and Rajma (Kidney Beans) before a 1000m downhill hike. His CGM showed three distinct spikes: first the sugar, then the rice, then the rajma. It was a vivid demonstration of how different carbohydrates digest at different speeds.
stories.insight: Complex carbs (Rajma) really do digest slower than simple starches (Rice) and sugar. You can see the physics of digestion in real-time.

stories.topic: Ancel Keys and the Sugar Lobby
stories.summary: Ancel Keys cherry-picked data in his 'Seven Countries Study' to blame saturated fat for heart disease, ignoring countries like France (high fat, low heart disease). This led to the low-fat/high-carb guidelines of the late 20th century, which Amit argues caused the obesity epidemic. The sugar lobby actively suppressed contrary research.
stories.insight: Scientific consensus can be manufactured by interest groups and bad methodology. The 'low fat' dogma was a disaster for public health.

stories.summary: Amit recounts a story from a former colleague, Sanhita, who said Ajay was a 'monster' to work with and made her cry often. But she also said she learned so much and would work with him again.
stories.insight: High standards can be painful but educational. (Though Amit frames it as a playful roast).

recommendations.author: Gary Taubes
recommendations.context: The central book for the episode.
recommendations.reason: Argues that sugar is the prime cause of diabetes and obesity, not just 'calories'. Compares sugar to tobacco in terms of public health impact.

recommendations.author: Nina Teicholz
recommendations.reason: Busts the myth that saturated fat causes heart disease.

recommendations.author: Dr. Jason Fung
recommendations.reason: Explains the role of insulin resistance and how fasting can reverse it.

recommendations.author: David Remnick
recommendations.context: On the fall of the Soviet Union.
recommendations.reason: A brilliant account of the collapse of an empire. Reminds us that the 'rule of law' is a 500-year project.

recommendations.author: Coomi Kapoor
recommendations.reason: Important history to remember how fragile democracy is. 'If the Emergency were on today, you and I would be in jail.'

core_ideas.concept: A Calorie is Not a Calorie
core_ideas.explanation: 100 calories of sugar spikes insulin and stores fat. 100 calories of complex carbs feeds the gut microbiome. The metabolic effect is totally different despite equal energy content.
Every time you eat (especially carbs), insulin spikes. Frequent spikes lead to resistance, which leads to diabetes. The solution is to lower insulin frequency (fasting) and intensity (low carb).
Eating fiber/protein before carbs slows down sugar absorption. The 'Western' order of salad -> main -> dessert is actually metabolically sound.
A Louis CK concept: Eating a full meal at one restaurant, then immediately going to another restaurant for a second full meal. Amit used to do this with Biryani and Pizza.

jokes_and_cultural_references.content: Amit jokes that they could have called the show 'Amit and Shah' (referencing the Indian politician Amit Shah).
Amit says if there is a cheesecake in the fridge, it will end up inside you. 'Please choose the option of the cheesecake being inside you, rather than you being inside the cheesecake.'
